# scored run; it does not put a value down the wire. `margin_row.tableau_f32`

# no yaml at all, so it was worth exactly zero in competition until somebody
# happened to look. It is now armed by `configs/vnncomp25/tinyimagenet_2024.yaml`
# and is therefore absent from this file. Everything below is in the state

# env-only debt to zero by PROMOTING levers in bulk, and the batch was required
# to be byte-identical on every scored run, so every promoted key had to ship
# unarmed. This file is the receipt for that promise AND the standing list of
# Adding a promotion adds a line here (one line, deliberate). Arming a key
# REMOVES its line, in the commit that carries the measurement justifying it.
# SCOPE: this census iterates `ny_levers::space::axes()` — the SEARCHABLE list
# only. Eight axes in `UNSAFE_AXES` also carry `Deliver::PresetKey` (the
# margin_row reserve/release/thread family among them) and are deliberately
# absent here: an unsafe axis is excluded from search by design, so its
# unarmed state is not debt. A text scan of space.rs that sweeps every
# `Axis {}` block counts them anyway and inflates this file by exactly 8 —
# that happened once, on 2026-08-27, and the ratchet's STALE rows caught it.
# Regenerate this file ONLY from the ratchet's own failure output, never from
# The registry class column is re-checked against `ny_levers::space::axes()` on

#bi-patch: promoted DARK and deliverable; no shipped yaml sets this key, and lever_delivery_pin_tests pins it absent from every shipped yaml. It cannot silently disconnect an armed key: it is a NEW Bool key (declaration default false) that overrides, rebuilds or clears no other key's value; unset, BiState::new builds no patch config, tighten_layer and the joint refresh never build a plan and run the same passes byte-identically, and the [bi-patch] prints are gated on the phase AND patch mode being armed; its readers are the backward-interm phase and #joint-refresh, both behind the space.rs edge (requires NY_MARGIN_ROW_BACKWARD_INTERM armed), and BackwardIntermRuntimePolicy::from_config pins it off so #rebake rounds stay dense. Armed, each prefix pair is a per-column receptive-field walk that is the dense pair restricted to its support (never looser, certified on its own; transposed convs, unequal-stride unions, beta-carrying overrides and planner tripwires fall back to the crop or the dense pair), and it prints [bi-patch] armed, a per-layer [bi-patch] plan line, then a [bi-patch] done: pairs= receipt (armed with pairs=0 is VOID). #auto-alloc prices the phase at the patch MACs only when this key is armed in the preset. Arming it removes this row, in the commit carrying the zero-NY_* yaml-route arrival proof, the cct CTL/W/P/PIA/PJ A/B and the moat.

#bi-window (cct plan P5 step 1): promoted DARK and deliverable; no shipped yaml sets this key, and lever_delivery_pin_tests pins it absent from every shipped yaml. It cannot silently disconnect an armed key: it is a NEW Bool key (declaration default false) that overrides, rebuilds or clears no other key's value; unset, BiState::tighten_layer runs the same dense seed and the same passes byte-identically and the [bi-window] prints are gated on the phase AND the crop being armed; its readers are the backward-interm phase, #joint-refresh and #root-certify-once (itself promoted DARK; it echoes the flag on its start line and passes it to its untrusted and certified intermediate refreshes, both gated on refresh_on, which requires backward-interm armed), so every pass that consumes it sits behind the space.rs edge (requires NY_MARGIN_ROW_BACKWARD_INTERM armed), and BackwardIntermRuntimePolicy::from_config pins it false so #rebake rounds stay dense. Armed, each cropped prefix pair is a certified pass of the unchanged engine on a net that computes exactly the seeded pre-activations (never looser than the dense pair; residual Add/Flatten/Gemm, transposed-conv and multi-consumer prefixes fall back dense) and prints [bi-window] armed then a [bi-window] done pairs= fallbacks= receipt (armed with pairs=0 is VOID). Arming it removes this row, in the commit carrying the zero-NY_* yaml-route arrival proof, the cct CTL/W/WJ/WJ0 x3 A/B and the moat.

promoted and deliverable; no shipped yaml sets this key, so the head-split Clip-and-Verify half resolves at its declaration default (off) on every scored run. Cannot silently disconnect an armed key: OFF is byte-identical by construction -- pack_from_rows computes no head slack at all when the gate is dark, so YPack::head_slack stays None and the eval site is never entered (head_clip_is_byte_identical_when_dark). ARMED, it says out loud whether it engaged: [clip-head] armed once per process on the first true resolution, then per-eval call= lines, then a lane-exit done= receipt with an explicit ARMED BUT INERT line when no evaluated domain ever carried a head fix -- so hs=0 everywhere reads as VOID rather than as a negative. SOUND: every halfspace is a necessary condition of a head sign fix the domain has already made, built from the y-pack's own certified line MINUS the slack recovered against the UNTIGHTENED forward concretization (never ly0 after clip_tighten_pack, never the ancestor-intersected entry box), with a rounding pad added so an over-recovery can only loosen and a NEGATIVE recovery refusing the whole pack rather than clamping (head_slack_calibration_must_use_fresh_concretization, head_frame_gate_refuses_a_transposed_or_shifted_pack); deltas come from the untouched ybox_deltas dual, non-negative by construction, and commit with max/min against the forward base, and a crossed interval is REFUSED and counted rather than read as an emptiness certificate (head_clip_encloses_the_true_subdomain, head_halfspace_on_exact_affine_head_does_not_cut_the_true_subdomain, dropping_the_head_slack_cuts_into_the_true_subdomain). Promoted because the whole clip family was env-only and run_instance.sh exports no NY_*, so no scored run could arm it. Arming it removes this row, in the commit carrying the measurement.

#wide-fd-search (ENGINE_PROGRAM M4): promoted DARK and deliverable; no shipped yaml sets this key. `f64` (default) is the frozen-dual tier's own f64 search bit for bit (no backend consulted); `cpu_f32` / `cuda` / `auto` hand each level's SCORING to the injected untrusted backend (ny-bbe CPU f32 SIMD; ny-cuda's device kernels, bit-identical to it and fail-soft) whose proposed dual points the tier certifies in f64 with its own block evaluator (pruned only on certified > 0; a refuted node is split, never pruned; the level ledger counts certified prunes only); it prints [bbe] armed=1 backend= probe= lease_mb= once per armed tier and search= probe= claimed= refuted= fallback= on every class line (an armed non-f64 run without them is VOID). Arming it removes this row, in the commit carrying the yaml-route arrival proof, the certified nodes/s measurement (S1), the refuted/claimed rate, the ctl-vs-armed x3 measurement and the both-year moat.

#frozen-dual-bab: deliverable manual tuning key, absent from shipped yaml. #fd-shared-state (ENGINE_PROGRAM M3): promoted DARK and deliverable; no shipped yaml sets this key. `per_class` (default) is today's frozen-dual tier bit for bit (one full state build per class inside its fair share); `shared` prices two slope candidates by one-column margin passes, builds every unstable row ONCE under the winner before the fair shares are computed, and gives each class a one-column margin tail over that trunk; it prints [frozen-dual] trunk state=shared lambda= ... on every shared tier run (an armed run without it is VOID). Inert unless margin_row.frozen_dual_bab is armed. Arming it removes this row, in the commit carrying the yaml-route arrival proof, the shared-lambda root-loss and classes-built measurement (t8853, t4863, FDB6, 10 E1-26 tiny rows x3), the tier-engaged sat negative controls and the both-year moat.
